title: Ship the Image: ECR, Fargate & the Load Balancer
subtitle: Learn the difference between an image, a task definition, a running task and a service.
analogy: The image is a sealed software package, the task definition is a launch form, a task is one running copy, and the service keeps the requested number of copies alive.
objectives: Build and publish an immutable, architecture-matched image.
Create API and worker task definitions using the same image.
Run a migration task before starting the services.
Explain ALB target health, readiness, deployment and rollback.
prerequisites: Complete the manual network/data/role setup, or follow the complete Terraform path in Chapter 8 instead.
Commit your app changes first so the Git SHA names the code actually built.

lessons.title: Image versus running infrastructure
body: An image tag selects a version; an image digest identifies exact image content. Task definitions are versioned launch configuration. Updating an ECR tag alone does not update an already running task; register a new revision and update the service.
Build linux/amd64 for this course’s X86_64 tasks and t3 hosts. ARM64 is also valid when the image and task/host architecture match; do not mix architectures accidentally.

lessons.title: ALB health and graceful deployments
body: Fargate awsvpc tasks have their own private IPs, so the target group uses target_type=ip. The lab target is port 8000 and /ready. /health is process liveness; /ready checks the database. A healthy task does not prove that a background job has completed.

Use a startup grace period, connection draining, and a deployment circuit breaker. Rollback requires a previous completed deployment; a first deployment with no healthy revision has nothing to roll back to.

lessons.title: Deploy in dependency order
body: Create network/data/roles and an ECR repository. Push the image. Register task definitions. Run python -m app.migrate once using the API definition with a command override. Verify exit code 0, then start API and worker services.
Schema migrations are a deployment concern. A growing system needs backward-compatible changes so old and new tasks can overlap during rolling deployment.

lessons.title: The HTTP boundary
body: The public ALB terminates client connections; it forwards only API requests, never worker jobs. The lab uses HTTP to avoid requiring a domain. Before real users, attach an ACM certificate, use HTTPS and add authentication/rate limiting.

handHoldingSteps: Create ECR bootcamp-manual-app with immutable tags and create log group /ecs/bootcamp-manual. Build and push the committed source with the commands below.

Replace every placeholder in the task definition. Register the API revision. Make a worker definition from the same image: name worker, command taskiq worker app.tasks:broker, no portMappings, and a worker log stream prefix.

Create ECS cluster bootcamp-manual-cluster. Run the API task definition once with command python -m app.migrate in private subnets/app-sg, no public IP. Inspect its stopped reason and api container exit code before proceeding.
Create an IP target group on 8000 with /ready, then a public ALB across both public subnets. Forward listener port 80 to the target group.
Create an API Fargate service with two tasks and the ALB attachment; create a worker service with one task and no ALB. Set 60-second health-check grace and deployment circuit-breaker rollback.
Test /enqueue using a JSON body through the ALB and wait for /jobs. Inspect logs for the same job ID rather than relying only on the service’s running count.
concepts: Image immutability: A new Git SHA tag is a new release; do not deploy a mutable latest tag.
Task definition: Configuration is versioned independently from running service instances.
Readiness: ALB checks only whether a target should receive traffic, not whether all business functions are healthy.

commands.command:
aws ecr create-repository --repository-name bootcamp-manual-app --image-tag-mutability IMMUTABLE
aws logs create-log-group --log-group-name /ecs/bootcamp-manual
ECR_URL=$(aws ecr describe-repositories --repository-names bootcamp-manual-app --query 'repositories[0].repositoryUri' --output text)
IMAGE_TAG=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
REGISTRY="${ECR_URL%%/*}"
aws ecr get-login-password --region "$AWS_REGION" | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin "$REGISTRY"
docker build --platform linux/amd64 -t "$ECR_URL:$IMAGE_TAG" .
docker push "$ECR_URL:$IMAGE_TAG"
commands.explanation: Run from the backend root, after committing changes. Create resources only once; describe existing resources on later releases.
commands.expected: An image tagged with the source Git SHA exists in ECR.

commands.command:
aws ecs register-task-definition --cli-input-json file://task-definition.json
aws ecs list-tasks --cluster bootcamp-manual-cluster
aws logs tail /ecs/bootcamp-manual --since 10m --follow
commands.explanation: Save the edited task definition as task-definition.json. Inspect tasks and logs while deploying.
commands.expected: The task-definition ARN includes a revision; logs show application startup.

commands.command:
curl -i -X POST "http://YOUR_ALB_DNS/enqueue" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"hello cloud"}'
sleep 3
curl -s "http://YOUR_ALB_DNS/jobs"
commands.explanation: Use the manual ALB DNS name, not a private task address.
commands.expected: 202 followed by a completed word-count result.

codeFiles.description: Complete manual API definition. Replace account IDs, image tag, roles, secret ARN, and endpoints. Create the log group first.

walkthrough.title: awsvpc and target type
walkthrough.explanation: Every Fargate task receives a private network interface. The ALB registers that IP and container port.

walkthrough.title: command
walkthrough.explanation: The image already contains an environment with uvicorn on PATH. Use the package path app.main:app, not the old main:app.

walkthrough.title: logging and secrets
walkthrough.explanation: awslogs needs the execution-role policy and a pre-existing log group. A DB_PASSWORD JSON-key ARN requires a compatible Fargate platform version; current Linux 1.4+ supports it.

architectureDescription: ECR supplies the image; task definitions describe the API and worker; Fargate starts them privately. The ALB routes HTTP only to API targets. The worker does not have an ALB connection.

breakItDrill.title: Break the readiness path
breakItDrill.scenario: Change the target health path to /not-found in the manual lab.
breakItDrill.symptom: Targets fail health checks even though the application process is running.
breakItDrill.fix: Restore /ready, verify database reachability, and observe healthy targets.

assignment.title: Perform a controlled release
assignment.description: Change the application title, commit, build a new SHA image and deploy a new task-definition revision. Explain how you would choose a known-good image for rollback.
assignment.completionHint: Verify the result yourself, then complete the chapter checklist.

recallNote.keyTakeaway: Publish the image, migrate the schema, then start and verify the services.
bullets: Fargate uses awsvpc and IP target groups.
Worker services have no public listener or load balancer.
A task count is not an end-to-end success check.

checklist.text: Build and publish an immutable, architecture-matched image.
Create API and worker task definitions using the same image.
Run a migration task before starting the services.
Explain ALB target health, readiness, deployment and rollback.
